column1: # The big step of 24. 11. 2026: samples for Richard first (the PA pole, the PDA in the hand).

column4: Pixel-art game sprite in the style of 1990s Build-engine games (Duke Nukem 3D, Redneck Rampage): chunky visible pixels, a limited muted palette, strong simple shading, a single object in the centre, full height. Background must be flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF everywhere around it, no ground shadow, no floor, no text, no border, no watermark. A village public address pole from 1980s Czechoslovakia (obecni rozhlas) seen from the front: a tall weathered grey concrete pole, near its top a rusty steel bracket holding two old grey metal horn loudspeakers pointing left and right and slightly down, their bells dented and streaked with rust, a black cable running down the pole to a small grey junction box with a hinged lid halfway down, a ceramic insulator, flaking paint, bird droppings on the bracket.

Pixel-art first-person sprite exactly like the hand and weapon sprites of a 1990s Build-engine game (Duke Nukem 3D, Blood, Redneck Rampage), matching the reference image EXACTLY in its glove, sleeve, skin, pixel size and shading. Seen from the player's own eyes. The player's LEFT hand in the same worn tan leather work glove, the forearm in the same rolled-up grey work-shirt sleeve coming up from the bottom LEFT edge of the frame, holding up in front of the view, upright and facing us, a grey plastic 1998 pocket computer (a Windows CE palmtop like a Psion or an early Palm): a chunky scuffed grey case with rounded corners, a large rectangular monochrome LCD screen taking most of its face, the screen plain empty pale grey-green with nothing on it, four small round grey buttons under the screen, a stylus slot on its side. The screen faces us squarely and fills a big part of the picture. Chunky pixels, strong simple shading, low saturation. Background must be flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF everywhere around the hand and the device, no shadow, no text on the screen, no logo, no border.

The screen faces us squarely and fills a big part of the picture. Chunky pixels, strong simple shading, low saturation. Background must be flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF everywhere around the hand and the device, no shadow, no text on the screen, no logo, no border.

An isometric building sprite for a late-1990s camp tycoon game in the style of the reference image: 2:1 isometric pixel art seen from the south-west, the same scale, palette, weathered textures and soft top-left light as the reference, a small dark shadow on the ground under it. The object stands alone on a flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) background, no ground tile, no text, no border. The object: a tall weathered grey concrete village public address pole from 1980s Czechoslovakia, near its top a rusty steel bracket holding two old grey metal horn loudspeakers pointing left and right, a thin black cable running down the pole to a small grey junction box at chest height.

A sheet of five small icons for the screen of a 1998 palmtop computer with a grey-green monochrome STN LCD: chunky hand-made 1-bit pixel art, pure black pixels only, no grey, no anti-aliasing, no outlines of other colours, each icon about 32 by 32 pixels with clear simple shapes, arranged in one row of five with wide even gaps, on a flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) background everywhere, no text, no numbers, no border, no frame. From left to right: a folded paper site map with a round pin; a bell with a small envelope beside it; a clipboard with a ticked checklist; an alarm clock with a small sun and cloud beside it; a snake made of square blocks curling toward a small apple.

A worn beige plastic 1990s dot-matrix printer seen from the front and a little above: a wide low box with a smoked plastic lid, a round platen knob on the right side, two small green indicator lights and a row of small square buttons on the front, a stack of pale green-striped continuous tractor-feed paper with perforated edges going in at the back, nothing coming out of it.
